# EE003 needs to send this payment back. 
# Any transaction recorded on IT001 side needs to be canceled. 
# For next intercompany invoices, BEFORE anything is created on IT001 side, I have to switch off a few intercompany settings. Same for EE003 when creating the supplier invoice. It’s also *superimportant* to coordinate this activity because before I switch off these settings, I need to notify accounting team to not make any intercompany invoices and/or transactions (because this will cause future errors and issues). And, the invoice needs to be in a bigger amount than the two ones so they could be netted against each other. Or net one by one, up to you. Intercompany settings also need to be switched off for when Settlement Run is created and payment is recor

Hei, we completely understand, we want to have good relationships with authorities, but at the same time we need to balance it with protecting the privacy of our users and also the potential public fallout if we release info without questioning what is being asked (especially when we bring third parties like fleet owners into the mix). 

I think what might help here is to make sure they know we're happy to cooperate and will help as much as we legally can and are obligated to. What might help us to narrow the initial list from the location of the attack, then start from there - who are we looking for? We know the potential attacker was on a scooter (can we filter out couriers with cars?); do we know any other locations they were seen outside coming in or our the area of attack; do we know the exact time the potential attacker was in specific are so we can narrow the location + timeframe) etc. This will help us hugely to specify the area we'll pull data from and we've better-documented trail that we've done our due diligence here. 

Often the police don’t know what data and how we collect so they go very broad with their requests, but we can help to make their request and our result way more specific = we find the better balance.

Hi Tanel, 

This is a good point and I will try to add it somewhere in the confluence page. The application can be different by affiliate but in short, by signing up on Awin, they will have a referral link that includes their unique ID. Based on the type of affiliate, they would either:

* share this link with their contacts/network whether it’s by traditional comms (emails, texts, WA), or via social media. 
* link up to a web banner or a button if they own a website. Example with an [+existing affiliate+|https://www.raspberryone.co.za/]
* place a physical banner in their physical site which include a QR code that integrates their link

Traditionally affiliates are influencers, bloggers, coupon pages. We take a different approach where we see the possibility for anyone to become an affiliate, including fuel stations, car maintenance companies, car rental websites etc.

Also note an important part is that affiliates receive payments from Awin, not directly Bolt. We give Awin the money needed to pay affiliates based on success criteria and compensation we agree beforehand, for example €20 per activation. This should be seen as a marketing channel rather than a service we’re asking them to do. We also don’t put any KPI or force them to bring in new drivers weekly.

Please note that the T&C has been written by Marja-Liisa Soone and Helena Rachao from Tax was actively involved before we go live.

If you have any questions please let me know.

Many thanks

Yes it means exactly that because Bolt is a platform operator, not the provider of the transportation service. 

However Users can benefit from insurance (i) taken up by the independent service provider, e.g driver, in the limits set by the applicable law, and (ii) if applicable in the relevant territory, Bolt has set up to cover damage caused to Users.

E.g in EU mandatory motor third party liability (MTPL - _liikluskindlustus_) policies are a requirement for all drivers directly, supported by state-facilitated fallback mechanisms. Harmonized by EU directive, all driver civil liability is covered under MTPL policy with minimum coverage of 1.2M for property and 5.6M for health damage per event. Covers damage caused to third parties and third-party property, but also to passengers.

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2], 

Thanks for your patience with this. Just to clarify some points for Sweden: 

* There is a strict requirement to obtain “+*explicit consent*+” from the consumer. Such explicit consent is usually obtained by way of actively pressing a consent button or by signing a consent form. However, obtaining this explicit consent from the consumer orally is not impossible but it needs to be a clear case. 
* The driver is responsible if consent has not been obtained properly and/or if the consent cannot be proven. This means that if the consumer denies that any consent has been given, it will be the driver who needs to provide proof that consent indeed was provided. In practice this will probably mean that we need to reimburse all cases where the consumer denies having given consent because the burden of proof in this case is quite high. 

Generally, we would not strictly need a consent button but from a practical point of view we should still consider it in my opinion.

When it comes to FI and NO, do you know if any multiple stop feature is active on the market and do you know if any previous review of the consent requirements have been done? I remember a colleague mentioning such a review for FI so just want to check if you were involved. 

Thanks!

Hey [~accountid:615d90da9cdb93007288f515]! 

Overall the legal team does not support such practice. The couriers' employment agreement with a company is irrelevant to Bolt since we are not a party to such an agreement. We cannot directly engage third parties' employees- it can give rise to employee misclassification risk (couriers may be considered Bolt employees) and tax consequences for Bolt. If we transfer payments to the courier’s bank accounts without any legal ground (an employment agreement with the unrelated party is not sufficient), we might be indirectly contributing to tax avoidance (for the tax team [~accountid:61b9ad7c2900b00071da0b68] to comment). Besides, the employment agreement cannot be relied upon to bind the company into the provision of services through its couriers since the company has not consented to that. 

If we want to engage the company that employs couriers, the best way is +to enter into an agreement with that company and make all the payments to its bank account.+ In this case, the company would be responsible for further payment of salaries to couriers and tax compliance. 

If an agreement with the company is not the best solution, we can +engage couriers only if they are registered as individual entrepreneurs+ and handle their own tax matters. [~accountid:61b9ad7c2900b00071da0b68] please comment if you support such an approach. 

[~accountid:615d90da9cdb93007288f515] is there any specific reason why you opted for engaging couriers based on an employment agreement with an unrelated company?

[~accountid:6068291caee2400068a2e2fb] clause 8.3 provides that “_The Partner has the right to terminate the Agreement without cause at any time by giving notice at least 30 days in advance. Bolt has the right to terminate the Agreement with Partner at any time by giving reasoned notice at least 30 days in advance. Bolt shall not notify the Partner of termination in advance if Bolt:_ 

_8.3.1 is subject to a legal or regulatory obligation which requires Bolt to terminate the provision of the whole of its online intermediation services to a given Partner in a manner which does not allow Bolt to respect that notice period; or_ 

_8.3.2 exercises a right of termination under an imperative reason pursuant to national law; or_ 

_8.3.3 can demonstrate that the Partner concerned has repeatedly infringed these General Terms, resulting in the termination of the provision of the whole of the online intermediation services in question.”_

The above entitles both parties to a 30 days prior notice before termination. *Clause 8.3* provides for termination with notice while *clause 8.4* provides for termination without notice.

Hey everyone,

I think that we reached the point where a business decision needs to be made as to what are the next steps. As I see it, we have the following options:

# not charge commission on refunds
## To me this sounds like the most reasonable approach. Our T&Cs section 5.1 sentence 2 states that we charge commission only if ride was completed. If there was no ride (or if the ride has been refunded), we shouldn’t charge the commission.
# charge commission on refunds if the driver is at fault
## This is not a risk-free approach but if we opt for this, then we would be able to say that driver still used our platform services under the T&Cs and this is what the driver has been charged for. I would say that this approach will bring about some angry drivers but this would be defendable to some extent in court. Should we opt for this approach, we should delete section 5.1 sentence 2 from our T&Cs as it is not compliant with the approach.

# 1.9. Bolt Fee – the fee that Driver is obliged to pay to Bolt +*for using the Bolt Platform*+*.*
# 4.13. Cancellation fee & wait time fee. Passenger may cancel a request for Transportation Services that a Driver has accepted via the Bolt App. In some markets, +*Driver may be entitled to the Fare for cancelled Transportation Services*+ (Cancellation Fee) in the event that a Passenger cancels accepted request for Transportation Services after a certain time period determined by Bolt App.

The argumentation here is the following - the Driver receives *the Fare* for the cancelled ride (clause 5.1 of the T&Cs), the Driver has to pay the Bolt Fee *on the Fare* (clauses 1.9, 5.1 of the T&Cs). That is why we charge the commision on the cancellation fee - the driver used our platform to earn the fare, and we are entitled to the commision.

Hi Erik, and thanks for the nudge here.

I've reviewed the following documents:

1. The certificate of analysis pertaining to emissions testing. This says that it has been done in accordance of Art.20 of TPD; however, Art.20 does not cover these kinds of products. However, in this case this refers to the method (aerosol capture, inhalation topography and analytical methods) used rather than the regulation applicable to the product. The analysis did not detect the presence of nicotine in the aerosol.

2. The MSDS is fairly standard. However, I'd want to be sure that the use of such a high concentration of silica is safe in a product intended for heating and inhalation. The manufacturer should have performed a toxicological risk assessment and be able to share it with us.

3. Marketing material which indicates that the product is for use in tobacco heating products like iQOS. I would want assurance from the manufacturer that they do not infringe on any patents, trademarks or other IP held by either PMI or BAT, and for them to indemnify Bolt against any action relating to patent infringement from any major tobacco company. Tobacco companies can be vicious when it comes to IP infringement.

I have seen lots of similar products come and go in the decade I worked in this space, and not really noticed any that have made an impact, and so I would temper your expectations as to the kind of volume this will do: people will buy it once as a novelty and then probably not buy it again. 

But, assuming the marketing is accurate and there is no combustion, it cannot be considered a herbal product for smoking, which is the only TPD category it might potentially fall into. If the manufacturer is able to give the assurance that it is not a herbal product for smoking (because it does not combust and therefore cannot produce smoke), along with the IP and toxicological assurances outlined above, I think you are relatively comfortable.

Please see below the comments on the lease agreement. Since we don’t have an editable version of the agreement we can’t do the changes directly in the document so either we need to forward the comments to the landlord or request an editable version so we can make the required changes. 

+*Clauses 1.2 and 2.1:*+ It is solely stipulated that the leased premises may be used for workshop and office. It must be specified that the premises may +also+ be used for storage.

+*Clause 2.2, 2.4 and 2.6*+ The wording in red must be added to clauses 2.2 and 2.4 as illustrated:

_2.2 - Udlejer indestår for, at anvendelsen af det lejede til det ovenfor angivne erhverv på ikrafttrædelsestidspunktet, jf. § 3.1,_ {color:#ff5630}_er lovlig og_ {color}_ikke strider mod lokalplan eller anden offentlig planlægning._

_2.4 - Lejer har_ {color:#ff5630}_efter ikrafttrædelsestidspunktet_{color} _ansvaret for, at den aftalte anvendelse ikke omfattes af særlige offentlige forskrifter og har pligt til at indhente og opretholde alle tilladelser, der kræves med hensyn til det lejedes indretning og drift, herunder forskrifter    vedrørende miljø- og brandforhold. Udlejer skal uden ugrundet ophold underrettes om myndighedskrav og modtage kopi af de fornødne tilladelser._

Clause 2.6 should be deleted in full as this includes a disclaimer (for the landlord) of any responsibility as regards to the overall agreed use being compliant with public regulations, registered easements on the property etc. (with reference to the tenant’s prior due diligence as regards to these matters). We can’t accept such a full disclaimer. 

+*Clause 4.5:*+ Bolt’s statutory right to damages (under the Danish Business Lease Act) - in case of the landlord’s (non-breach) termination is capped at an amount equal to 1 months’ rent. We recommend that the cap is either deleted or alternatively increased to an amount equal to 6 months’ rent.

+*Clause 7 (and appendix 2) + clause 8 (and appendix 2.1)*+

According to appendix 2 (specification of joint utility expenses) the basis of distribution related to the leased premises is 527/*4,259*. According to the appendix the stipulated costs are the costs related to “the whole property” (4,259 sqm).

However, according to appendix 2.1 (specification of joint operating expenses) the basis of distribution related to the leased premises is 527/*10,218*. Here, the denominator of the fraction is (again) described as the acreage of “the whole property”.

The lease agreement does not include any explanation as regards to the use of +two different denominators+. This should be clarified.

+*Clause 9.1*+ The rent is to be adjusted according to the Danish Net Price Index, however with a minimum of 3 %. I recommend that the minimum adjustments is deleted, or alternatively that a cap of 5 % is added if the minimum adjustment remains.

+*Clause 10.1 and 10.2*+

Clause 10.1: I recommend adding a mutual protection period for adjustment to market rent equal to the agreed non-terminability period. Meaning, protection period until the end of March 2028.

Clause 10.2: I recommend that this is deleted in full. It is not market terms that an adjustment to market rent is effected all at once. According to the Danish Business Lease Act (and market terms) such adjustment is to be distributed over four years, so that the adjustment per year constitutes one quarter of the total adjustment.

Let me know if you have any questions on these comments. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

*Advice from Ilaria Moretti at Burness Paul re Clawback Agreement for Nursery Benefits:*

_'In relation to your first query about whether this should be included in the Employee Handbook we would agree with you that it would be best to keep this separate. We note that the Handbook does not set out all benefits that are on offer but states that they are listed on your UK Confluence page and so it would seem in keeping with this for the Nursery Benefit to be separate too._

_In relation to the use of a claw back agreement, whilst these are commonly used to recover sponsorship funding or training costs, we think the workplace nursery benefit is quite different to those. The most significant difference is that this benefit is set up as a salary sacrifice scheme and therefore there may be tax implications on any clawback arrangement._

_In our view, any clawback arrangement would have to be limited to the losses suffered as a result of the employee leaving part way through the contracted nursery year (i.e. recovery would be limited to the payments you would have to continue to make to the nursery after they have left), since any payments made before that are intended to be funded out of the company’s NI savings and so are not a direct cost to the business. The initial view from our tax team was that, whilst they don’t think that an arrangement in which an employee is required to make good to their employer any losses they suffer as a result of the salary sacrifice arrangement ending early would necessarily invalidate the salary sacrifice arrangement itself, there may be implications if the money recovered is not proportionate to the losses suffered. For example, you may save more than £100 each month in employer NIC’s and you would have to take account of that in any funds that you tried to recover from the employee. Failing to do so may mean that the repayment clause could be considered a penalty and could be unenforceable since it goes beyond recovering the actual loss suffered by the company._

_Our overarching view in light of above is that it may be quite heavy handed to claw back this particular benefit and the administrative burden of calculating the losses (and trying to recover payment) may not make it worth doing. That being said, if you would like us to provide a template agreement in any event please let us know and we can prepare this for you. Alternatively, if you would like our tax team to provide more specific advice on this please do let us know and we can arrange that.'_

*TL;DR.* This is how Survicate works. If we want to show a targeted survey upon the first page load, we should trigger it manually.

Long explanation below.

What happens is that we have a SPA, all the assets are injected in the first phase, for simplicity you can call it server-side rendering. 

In the subsequent phases we fetch data on the client side, including data required for targeting attributes. 

So, when we call {{setVisitorTraits}}, the initial HTML has already been loaded. I expected {{setVisitorTraits}} to check if there are surveys that had to be opened when the page was loaded, and open them. 

Evidently, this is not the case. The page loads, targeting attributes are yet to be set, so Survicate's script just exits as they're no surveys to show upon page load. Then we fetch data and set attributes but the ship has already sailed – surveys will be shown upon next page load event.
I’m closing this ticket at the moment. Please create a new ticket when we have all the approvals.

However, if Driver Score is available in PT, then I don’t see any increased risk if the Driver Score will be decreased if driver cancels the order less than an hour before the pickup. Driver is essentially breaching the transportation agreement with the rider in that case and, hence, abusing the platform. This is how Driver Score currently works for all the rides (not only for Scheduled Rides).

However, if we are not happy with decreased Driver Score for Scheduled Rides, then we shouldn’t be happy with Driver Score in general. Driver Score is essentially finding the signals where driver abuses transportation agreement with the rider or where driver or his/her behaviour is unsafe and decreases on the basis of that. Happy to discuss further if there are any questions.

Update werkzeug package from 2.2.2 to 2.2.3

Werkzeug's multipart form data parser will parse an unlimited number of parts, including file parts. Parts can be a small amount of bytes, but each requires CPU time to parse and may use more memory as Python data. If a request can be made to an endpoint that accesses {{request.data}}, {{request.form}}, {{request.files}}, or {{request.get_data(parse_form_data=False)}}, it can cause unexpectedly high resource usage.

This allows an attacker to cause a denial of service by sending crafted multipart data to an endpoint that will parse it. The amount of CPU time required can block worker processes from handling legitimate requests. The amount of RAM required can trigger an out of memory kill of the process. Unlimited file parts can use up memory and file handles. If many concurrent requests are sent continuously, this can exhaust or kill all available workers.

{noformat}SELECT
        bug.id AS business_user_group_id,
        bug.business_company_id AS business_company_id,
        bugul.id AS business_user_global_user_linking_id
FROM `business_user_global_user_linking` AS bugul
JOIN (SELECT business_user_id, business_user_group_id 
      FROM `business_user_group_membership`
      LIMIT 1000
      ) gm ON gm.business_user_id = bugul.business_user_id
JOIN `business_user_group` bug           ON bug.id = gm.business_user_group_id
WHERE 
        NOT EXISTS(
        SELECT 1 FROM `business_user_global_user_payment_method` AS payment
                WHERE (payment.global_user_id = bugul.id
                        AND payment.business_company_id = bug.business_company_id
                        AND payment.business_user_group_id = bug.id)
        )
limit 1000{noformat}

Hey! 

We have guidelines for these cases under the 3rd step:

* If the account cannot be archived, the system will let you know by showing an error message in Admin. It is REQUIRED that the CS agent informs the user requesting the deletion that the account cannot be archived:
** *_unpaid_orders_**:* the user has debt (negative balance) or failed payments in countries that do not have Bolt Balance (HU, AT). Advise the user to top up their balance in the app or (in HU, AT) retry the payment. 
** _ongoing_orders_: the user has a pending payment associated with a recent order. It's possible that the user has an active order or the recent order wasn't captured yet. Put the ticket _on-hold_ and try again in 72 hours. Inform the user that the account cannot be archived until the pending payment is processed and that a new attempt will be made in 72 hours. If you still receive the same error, submit a ticket to the Fraud team via [Service Desk.|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/-1] 
** _chargeback_payments:_ the amount of chargebacks exceeds the amount we allow. You can mention to the user that they’ve had multiple chargebacks due to which we can’t delete their account. If they explain the reasons for the chargebacks, submit a [Service Desk|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/-1] ticket to the Fraud team, put the ticket on-hold and await for the response. *Do not promise* the user that their account will be deleted before receiving a reply.
** _payment_problems_: inform the user that there are pending payment disputes and we’ll retain their account due to that according to our Privacy Policy.
** _same_phone_number_many_accounts_: in the last 6 months, the user has had 10+ accounts with the same phone number. *Do not give these details to the user.* Instead, inform them that irregularities on their account were detected and their account will be retained due to irregular activity according to our Privacy Policy.

In case of unpaid orders: advise the user to top up their balance. Once they’ve done it and came back to us, continue with the process as usual.

In case of fraud issues (e.g. chargeback payments) submit a ticket to the Fraud team and await for their response. 

These automations were requested by the Fraud/Commerce team and approved by the Legal team, so these can be trusted 🙂 Let me know if you have any questions!

Hi Carolina,

Options cannot be granted in the past - if the grant request is done late then custom vesting schedule is added to the grant to make sure that everything vests as if would have if the grant was made in a timely manner. Having said that then yes, option grant dates do not align with your promotional dates, but it’s not impacting vesting in that sense that you are also vesting your units later.

I’ll explain it below but just highlighting here that Bolt’s vesting period length is 4 years.

*Batch 2*

Promotional date: 1.08.2020
Grant date in Carta: 1.01.2021
Now if grant date would be 1.01.2021 and our usual 4 year vesting schedule (back then 6/48 semiannual, no cliff OR 6/48 semiannual, 1 year cliff) would be attached then that would mean that you would fully vest the grant on 31.12.2024. However, the vesting schedule attached to your grant is accustomed (12/7+6/36 semiannual, 7 months cliff) and if you look in at the actual vesting then you can see that it works as if the grant was granted to you on 1.08.2020 - grant becomes fully vested on 31.07.2024, which is 4 years -1 day from grant date/your promotional date.

*Batch 3*

Promotional date: 1.04.2021
Grant date in Carta: 27.06.2021
Grant request has been made by your then manager Lilia Konstantinova stating amount of units 400, and grant date 27.05.2021. Since the request again wasn’t made on time then we got to grant the units in June, with a date 27.06.2021 and accustomed the grant with a custom vesting schedule (3/48 quarterly, no cliff -1 months) making sure that the grant would vest as requested - grant becomes fully vested on 26.05.2025, which is 4 years -1 day from grant date.

All discrepancies should be addressed before accepting the grant. Due to legal and tax reasons no changes can be made for already accepted grants.

Kind regards

Hi [~accountid:626c24971a4eb30069d28197], 

We previously had a similar question about this for the SE market and we have a global approach to this so please see the description below. 

Such price changes will not be a _de facto_ change of the general T&Cs because the rates are not included in the terms. However, our global approach is that changes in e.g. commission is part of the T&C updates because the rates and price components are reflected in the app and in driver’s chat. So the following shall apply:

# No change of the general T&Cs are required, only update of the rates in the app.
# Since our approach is that this is an update of terms based on which we provide services to the drivers/riders, we need to follow the notification rules laid out in the P2B Regulation. Such changes to the terms need to be communicated to the business users at least 15 days in advance (Article 3 section 2). Exceptions can be made if (i) we need to do that very urgently and (ii) we are e.g. decreasing the commission which can be seen as a positive change which would make it possible to have a shorter notice period. 

For reference, please see wordings of article 3 section 2 below which applies to changes made in relation to the drivers:

_Providers of online intermediation services shall notify, on a durable medium, to the business users concerned any proposed changes of their terms and conditions_

_The proposed changes shall not be implemented before the expiry of a notice period which is reasonable and propor tionate to the nature and extent of the envisaged changes and to their consequences for the business user concerned. That notice period shall be at least 15 days from the date on which the provider of online intermediation services notifies the business users concerned about the proposed changes. Providers of online intermediation services shall grant longer notice periods when this is necessary to allow business users to make technical or commercial adaptations to comply with the changes._

The same notice period applies in relation to changes of terms affecting consumers i.e. riders. 

Let me know if you have additional questions. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

WITH last_unlinked_date AS (
  SELECT
    pmia.menu_item_id AS menu_id,
    MAX(pmia.last_update) AS menu_last_unlink_date
  FROM
    "ng_delivery"."delivery_menu_provider_menu_item_availability" pmia
  WHERE status = 'deleted'
  GROUP BY pmia.menu_item_id

last_5_menus_per_provider AS (
  SELECT
    a.provider_id, a.menu_item_id AS menu_id, a.last_update
  FROM (
    SELECT pmia.provider_id, pmia.menu_item_id, pmia.last_update,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY provider_id ORDER BY last_update DESC) rank_order
    FROM "ng_delivery"."delivery_menu_provider_menu_item_availability" pmia
    WHERE pmia.status = 'deleted'
  ) a
  WHERE a.rank_order <= 5
)
SELECT COUNT(id)
FROM (
  SELECT
    mi.id
  FROM last_unlinked_date m
  LEFT JOIN last_5_menus_per_provider last5 ON last5.menu_id = m.menu_id

  WHERE last5.menu_id IS NULL
    AND m.menu_last_unlink_date >= timestamp '2022-08-01' AND m.menu_last_unlink_date < current_date - interval '3' month
    AND mv.state IN ('discoverable')

    FROM "ng_delivery"."delivery_menu_menu_version" mv
    JOIN "ng_delivery"."delivery_menu_menu_item" mi ON mi.menu_id = mv.menu_id

*Problems with process logic:*

* Currently we assume that the driver is at fault but there can be situations where a driver has to take a longer route.
* _Check the market-specific driver compensation guidelines and request a manual adjustment to correct the driver's earnings, if applicable_ – what does if applicable mean? It’s not clear when and how drivers should be compensated.
* Is the second step of verifying if automation was applied needed? It kind of overlaps with step 3.
* Step 5 – why do we take complaints from within 3 months into account only in the UK? Why do we escalate to local Ops in Germany if there’s already one comment on the driver’s profile?
* Driver informs us about a road closure – the instructions are only about reporting but do we then compensate the driver as well?
* Comparing the tracking route vs predictive route does not mention any criteria, and therefore it’s prone to human error / bias.
* Using Google Maps to compare the route does not bring additional value as we cannot accurately confirm if that was the most efficient route at that moment.
** We do not have confirmation that the calculated route during prediction is the same as the route presented after starting the trip
** We are not aware what route was presented to the driver after starting the trip
** We are not aware which navigation app the driver used
* Overall we cannot accurately confirm bad intention from the driver side
* _“Longer route is not confirmed if”_ section is not clear whether any or all 3 conditions need to be met
* “_Longer route is not confirmed if: the price is as expected / predicted”_ - If the route is different but the price is as predicted, checking the route map is a redundant step.
* _“Longer route is confirmed if the compared routes are different and the price is higher than expected”_ - What if the routes are similar, but the price is still higher?
* _“If automation was applied, advise the rider that a promotion has been added to their account”_ - This is step 3. If the automation was already applied, manual route verification is unnecessary.
* Actioning the report does not specify the global timeframe for checking similar driver comments.
* In our blocking message to the drivers we mention: _“Please follow the route suggested by the Bolt app to avoid such complaints in the future”_ - However we are not aware how the Bolt app route looks like not we compare it to the actual during manual route verification.
* We don't have a threshold for how many times we can compensate a rider.
* In Estonia is unclear why is needed to escalate and what is the expected outcome
* In France the escalation process does not bring any value as agents are already leaving notes on the order page and in the ticket
** _“Ensure that the issue with the ride has not been reported already in their profile”_ - unclear instructions
* In Ukraine there is no mention of the timeframe for counting comments
* Under additional information about automation the overcharge amount criteria is unclear
** _“The rider has not had the same compensation in the last 30 days”_ - However we bypass automation by compensating the rider, which makes either the initial criteria or the CS process redundant
** Overall, the automation criteria are unclear



*Problems with the content:*

* _If the rider requests that the refund be made to their original payment method, use the Force full button_ – it’s not clear that force full refund is made on top of partial refund to Bolt Balance.
* Step 2 – would it make sense to create a separate article and link it instead of having this info in so many articles?
* Step 3 – would it make sense to differentiate the process depending on whether the automation was applied or not? If the automation was applied, then it doesn’t matter whether the longer route is confirmed or not so it could make the process a bit shorter.
* Step 5 – why is it called _Action the report?_ 
* Step 5 – inconsistency in the global and UA instructions for taking actions depending on the number of comments (global instructions are a test, UA ones are shown in a table).
* If market specifics are to stay, would it make sense to present them in a table like in this [article|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360010933439--Courier-wants-to-switch-cities]?
* Is additional information about automations useful? Should it be kept in this article or should it be a separate one?

* The process doesn’t mention following up with the driver, but the article contains a “*Driver informs us about a road closure*” section.

However, I just wanted to flag that for contracts like this (where we are the controller, it’s global in nature, covers processing of high risk data and is of high value) our starting position should be unlimited liability and if they push back EUR10million, then EUR5million and if they still don’t accept that then it’s a call for my team to make depending on type of data being processed.

For example the update should include: sub-processor details (the link included in MSA is no longer valid), Data Protection Officer details for both parties, frequency of transfers (no longer sufficient to say for duration of agreement), location of processing, the relevant supervisory authority, relevant EU governing law (cannot rely on England & Wales for EU processing as outside of EU) etc. This is legally required language and if not included means we risk any transfers not being lawfully protected by the SCCs.

Clevertap data:  debt notification messages

{noformat}with fragmented_events as 
	(
		select 
			eventname,
			ts,
			eventprops_campaign_id,
			eventprops_wzrk_id,
			eventdate,
			eventprops_campaign_type,
			t.profile_identity
		from clevertap.converted_clevertap_driver 
		cross join unnest(profile_all_identities) as t (profile_identity)
	),
	events_clevertap as 
	(
		select b.*
		from 
		(
			select 
				ccd.eventname,
				CAST(parse_datetime(CAST(ccd.ts AS varchar), 'yyyyMMddHHmmss') AS timestamp) AS event_timestamp,
				CASE WHEN ccd.eventname IN ('Notification Sent','Control Group')  THEN ccd.eventprops_campaign_id ELSE SPLIT_PART(ccd.eventprops_wzrk_id,'_', 1) END message_id,
		        CASE WHEN ccd.eventname IN ('Notification Sent','Control Group') THEN ccd.eventdate  ELSE DATE_PARSE(SPLIT_PART(ccd.eventprops_wzrk_id,'_', 2), '%Y%m%d') END sent_dt,
				ccd.eventprops_campaign_type,
				cast(replace(ccd.profile_identity, 'driver-', '') as bigint) as driver_id
			from fragmented_events ccd
			where regexp_like(ccd.profile_identity, 'driver-[0-9]*$')
				and ccd.eventname in ('Notification Sent', 'Notification Viewed', 'Notification Clicked','Control Group')
		) as b
		where regexp_like(b.message_id, '^[0-9]*$')
	),
	events_agg as 
	(
		select 
			cast(message_id as bigint) as message_id,
			driver_id,
			eventprops_campaign_type,
			sent_dt,
			count(*) as count_events,
			count(case when eventname = 'Notification Sent' then message_id end) as count_notif_sent,
			min(case when eventname = 'Notification Sent' then event_timestamp end) as earliest_notif_sent,
			max(case when eventname = 'Notification Sent' then event_timestamp end) as latest_notif_sent,
			count(case when eventname = 'Notification Viewed' then message_id end) as count_notif_viewed,
			min(case when eventname = 'Notification Viewed' then event_timestamp end) as earliest_notif_viewed,
			max(case when eventname = 'Notification Viewed' then event_timestamp end) as latest_notif_viewed,
			count(case when eventname = 'Notification Clicked' then message_id end) as count_notif_clicked,
			min(case when eventname = 'Notification Clicked' then event_timestamp end) as earliest_notif_clicked,
			max(case when eventname = 'Notification Clicked' then event_timestamp end) as latest_notif_clicked,
			count(case when eventname = 'Control Group' then message_id end) as count_control_group,
			min(case when eventname = 'Control Group' then event_timestamp end) as earliest_control_group,
			max(case when eventname = 'Control Group' then event_timestamp end) as latest_control_group
		from events_clevertap 
		group by 1, 2, 3, 4
	)
	select 
		ea.*,
		d.message_type,
		d.message_name,
		d.channel,
		d.delivery_type,
		d.conversion_event
	from events_agg ea
	left join ng_public.etl_clevertap_driver_campaign_journey_properties d on d.message_id = ea.message_id {noformat}

# Transporting foodstuff is okay - all the retailers have some warehouses, where the goods are taken in and distributed as the need rises. 
# To reduce the risks, the transportation service should be outsourced. This means, the contractor will be liable for ensuring the goods are kept in the right conditions during the transportation.
# From warehouse side the main risk is temperature control (chilled and cooled foodstuff). Smaller risk is everything related to packing the goods out, as this will be the main question, should anything be destroyed/ruined during the arrival.
# From transportation side - keeping the cold chain is the main concern. This means, special trucks/vans must be used. If we don’t have them, this should be outsourced. Purchase price of the vans is ~40k EUR for a new one and ~20k EUR for a used one.

*Block only documents expiring after:*
Blocks a driver only if their verified document of this type expires after the specified date. Verified documents expiring before this date will be treated as indefinitely valid. This setting will apply if the {{block if expired}} is enabled.

Example: lets say {{Block only documents expiring after}} is set to 15/03/2023. We have 2 verified documents with different expiry dates.

* for document 1 which has the expiry date as 01/03/2023, then document won't be considered for blocking as its expiry date is before the {{Block only documents expiring after}}. Hence no block will be scheduled
* Whereas for document 2 which has the expiry date as 16/03/2023, then document will be considered for blocking as its expiry date is after the {{Block only documents expiring after}}. Hence block will be scheduled starting from 16/03/2023 and reason would be {{document expired}}

*Block drivers after document expiry in days:* 

Delay blocking a driver by the specified number of days if the document of this type expires. For example, setting this to 7 would allow driver to continue working for 7 more days after the document expires without a new document. This settings applies only when {{block if expired}} is enabled

Example: lets say {{Block drivers after document expiry in days}} is set to 10. We have a document which expires on 16/03/2023. So now instead of applying the document block on 16/03/2023, Block would be applied from 26/03/2023 (16/03/2023 + 10 days). Hence the driver can now work for 10 more additional days

Hello @Michelle Rinaldo ! The main problem is that we received several complaints from our customers, who purchased our rental passes but cannot use them because the service terminated. We can cancel the pass and issue a full refund in case no more than 14 days passed after purchasing the pass. But there is no information in KB article nor in the Terms of service on how we should proceed if the user wants to cancel the pass because he could not use it due to the bad weather -> closing the service. When the users contact us, the pass can be active for more than 14 days already. And despite it and the fact that the user could use our service a lot during that time, they still want a refund or the remaining days to be re-calculated. Because they do not have the possibility to use the pass. 

So, regarding your question, I would say it is mostly related to the case, when the service is terminated in the entire city for a specific time-period due to bad weather (the users do not know for how much, and we do not inform them how long the service will be closed nor provide any information about what will happen with their pass). Because, as I see right now, in Norway (where the requests usually comes from), we do not close the season, but just stop the service for some time (day, two, several weeks) and then open it once the weather is good for using the scooters.

Engineering discourages using Looker to schedule data sendouts to external party. According to [~accountid:59f9f9024b3f596e0597748e], the main reasons are:

What happened:
-an RC uses something from common/campaigns
-now all the modules get that RC, and as a consequence they try to get the common/campaigns thing as well
-not all modules have common/campaigns reference, so they start to fail the build (not all of them, just those that don’t have  common/campaigns reference in their tsconfig)

Solution: not have all modules will include all gen folder by default,
but when a module wants to use and RC it should include the gen folder where that RC is defined (plus all the eventual dependencies

In general, DL suggests that the DBA team follow the below steps when migrating MySQL tables to TiDB:

# DBA creates the new changefeed if it’s a new TiCDC cluster
# DBA checks if the Kafka TiDB topics have events sent from the Tables migrated to TiDB
# DBA creates [https://github.com/bolteu/change-data-capture|https://github.com/bolteu/change-data-capture|smart-link]  PR.
# DL reviews and approves and merges the above PR.
# DBA runs the script (maintained by DBA) for data verification. DL has provided the criteria of the data verification in the {{Suggestions from Data Lake for verification}} of the above google doc.

Hi [~accountid:6257f8239770e600716a5307] apologies for keeping you waiting!



Re 3.1 of special terms: 

This conflicts with T&C-s clause 4.1 which states that parties act as separate data controllers.

Therefore would push back with the following explanation:

Bolt and Customer are deemed as separate data controllers under the Agreement (T&C-s clause 4.1). Therefore Bolt does not process the data of end users on behalf of the Customer as a processor, but as an individual data controller in order to provide services to the end users under the applicable Terms of Service.

If the Customer wishes to conclude a separate agreement regarding data processing between individual controllers, then we can use Bolt’s Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) (added to the ticket).

The fact that one organisation provides a service to another organisation does not necessarily mean that it is acting as a data processor. It could be a data controller in its own right, depending on the degree of control it exercises over the processing operation. Bolt as a controller decides the means and purposes for processing the data in order to provide the service (Bolt Business to the Customer). Bolt is the one registering and administering the users, providing the platform, providing the opportunity for end-users to make use of Bolt Business in the limits set by Customers. Therefore the data being shared is for each parties separate purposes - Bolt determines the means and purposes in order to provide the services and Customer determines the means and purposes of the shared data on how to manage their accounting purposes for business rides. 

Such conclusion and approach is also reflected in the guidance of [European Data Protection Board Guidelines|https://edpb.europa.eu/system/files/2021-07/eppb_guidelines_202007_controllerprocessor_final_en.pdf] (see p 82).

Hi [~accountid:62bbfa39ec4c0d377f9fc3b7] , I’m the GA for Finland. I can fill in on A/B test specifics. A/B tests typically show different riders different types of treatments - in our case different riders will get different prices. The control group will receive our regular price while the treatment will get the new price we want to test.



We generally use Price Modification constants (PMCs) to test prices. What happens is the upfront price or price shown to the rider is changed. We could also change components of the test like start fare, per km fare, per min fare, etc but generally it impacts all components except min price.

However, when we use PMCs for A/B test, the exact fare components in the breakdown will not change so if riders actually checked the breakdown before ordering a ride. As we aren’t permanently changing this yet, we also don’t want to change the fare components right away (although I have to check with devs if we have the option to test changing the components in the app too)

We should decline. As mentioned, Bolt is providing platform intermediary services and the drivers and couriers are independent third parties.

Regarding NO, Norwegian law does not set out any specific consent requirements as such for adding stops to a taxi ride. However, the right to claim additional payment for added stops will be conditional on the existence of an agreement, whether written or oral, between the driver and the passenger. This implies that passengers should be adequately informed in advance that adding stops will be subject to an increase in the original price, as well as of the exact price for adding stops. Thus, this should be adequately explained in Bolt's passenger general terms and conditions, as well as being addressed in the app (which is already the case). Ideally should such changes to the taxi ride be subject to some form of documentation or traceability, either in writing or in the app, to reduce the potential risks associated with passenger and drivers disagreeing as to added stops or new prices.

Hi Julia Kisseljova,

Apologies for the slow response and thanks for your understanding. 

[+Article L121-17+|https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000032227250] FR Consumer code states that  : “_prior to the conclusion of a contract of sale or provision of services,_ *_the trader shall ensure the express consent of the consumer for any additional payment added to the price of the main object of the contract._*

_In the event that the additional payment results from the consumer's consent given by default, i.e. in the absence of express opposition on his part to paid options that he has not requested, the consumer may claim reimbursement of the sums paid for this additional payment._”

The scope of the application of the above provisions is not straightforward. However, we are of the view that they would apply to the issue at stake and therefore express consent should be sought. 

In any case, the addition of a stop by the driver would be seen as an unilateral modification to the contract entered into between passenger and driver and, in the absence of a proper consent/ accept button, it will be *difficult to prove the formation of the amended contract* (i.e. the moment where the offer of modified journey is accepted by passenger).

Furthermore, in FR Bolt qualifies as “_centrale de réservation_” under Transportation Code and accordingly Bolt is jointly liable towards passengers for the proper performance of the service rendered by drivers. Failing the passenger’s express acceptance, it would be burdensome for Bolt to prove the existence of the amended contract, hence the scope of undertakings for which Bolt could be held jointly liable under local transportation law vis-a-vis passengers. 

In light of the above, I recommend implementing a specific button allowing passengers to accept or reject the additional stop as inserted by the driver. Passengers should be provided with the quote of the increased price before being able to accept/ decline the additional stop.

*Overall: Phone recording in germany*

*Based on a joint resolution of the German DPAs the recording of telephone conversations is generally only permissible under data protection law with the consent of the external conversation partner. Besides the necessary consent of the conversation partner, we should also check the proper legal bases regarding the recording of employees (see point 4 of the remarks) and also the necessary design of the recording process (retention time, information, amount of records,…).* _Some sources explicitly mention the German criminal code and recommend consent to avoid potential criminal charges_


*Remarks*

# *DSK-Resolution (in general)*
In the data protection conference (committee of the independent German data protection supervisory authorities of the federal and state governments), the data protection supervisory authorities of the federal and state governments agree on common positions. Their resolutions are positions that relate to the interpretation of data protection regulations or corresponding recommendations.

Such a resolution is currently available in connection with the recording of telephone calls (03/23/2018 - recording of telephone calls). Even if it is already 5 years old, it can still be accessed on the DSK homepage and there are no more recent resolutions on this topic on the homepage ([https://www.datenschutzkonferenz-online.de/beschluesse-dsk.html)|https://www.datenschutzkonferenz-online.de/beschluesse-dsk.html)|smart-link] )

# *Business-Partner/ Clients/ …*
*DSK Resolution on phone call recording:*[*https://www.datenschutzkonferenz-online.de/media/dskb/20180323_dskb_aufzeichnung_telefon.pdf*|https://www.datenschutzkonferenz-online.de/media/dskb/20180323_dskb_aufzeichnung_telefon.pdf]
_“The recording of telephone conversations is generally only permissible under data protection law with the consent of the external conversation partner. Effective consent under data protection law within the meaning of Art. 4 No. 11 DS-GVO requires that the external conversation partner is asked before the intended recording begins whether he or she agrees to the recording and, if he or she agrees, is asked to clearly express his or her consent, for example, by saying "yes" or by an active confirming action (such as pressing a telephone key). This consent does not include biometric evaluation. The mere granting of the possibility to object and the subsequent continuation of the telephone call do not constitute an effective consent under data protection law within the meaning of the GDPR. Since the data controller must be able to prove that the data subject has given effective consent (Art. 7(1) GDPR), he must also be able to prove that the data subject gave consent "in an informed manner" (cf. Art. 4 No. 11 GDPR).”_

# {color:#ffc400}*Art 6 Sec 2 lit b GDPR:*{color} CNIL-Opinion (25.04.2022): The recording of telephone conversations f*or the purpose of proving the conclusion of a contract is allowed to the extent necessary.* Therefore, a controller who wishes to record telephone conversations for evidential purposes must show that there are no other (lesser) means to prove the conclusion of the contract. It is therefore necessary to distinguish contracts that can be concluded orally from those for which the agreement must necessarily be established by a written contract.
”_Only telephone conversations for the conclusion of a contract may be recorded. The trader must therefore provide mechanisms to record the telephone conversation between the teleoperator and the consumer only from the moment when its subject clearly relates to the conclusion of a contract . The relevant part of the conversation can only be made in the absence of any other evidence of the conclusion of the contract or its performance, such as a written confirmation” (_[https://www.cnil.fr/fr/lenregistrement-des-conversations-telephoniques-afin-detablir-la-preuve-de-la-formation-dun-contrat|https://www.cnil.fr/fr/lenregistrement-des-conversations-telephoniques-afin-detablir-la-preuve-de-la-formation-dun-contrat|smart-link] _)_

# *Employees*
{color:#bf2600}*Legal Permission Paragraph 26 Sec 1 1. Sentence BDSG:*{color} With regard to employees, Paragraph 26 Sec 1 1. Sentence BDSG could initially be the legal permission, as the recording serves to monitor performance and conduct and thus the implementation of the employment relationship in the broader sense. Section 26 (1) sentence 1 BDSG states:
*_Personal data of employees may be processed for purposes of the employment relationship if this is necessary [...] after the establishment of the employment relationship for its implementation [...]._*

This means that the recording would have to be necessary in order to be able to achieve the purposes pursued with it (training, quality assurance). *Necessary means that there should be no milder means to achieve the stated purposes.* In my opinion this is not the case, since call centre operators and customer support have other and milder means at their disposal (listening in of telephone calls or mystery calls). Even if the recording can potentially be more effective than these two means of control, within the framework of proportionality and against the background of the intensity of the intervention of the voice recording, the interest of the employee worthy of protection is to be assessed higher than the interest of the customer support manager in a third possibility of control through voice recording.

{color:#36b37e}*Consent:* {color}In principle, consent in the context of employment relationships must be critically evaluated as a basis for permission, since due to the special relationship of dependency between employer and employee, it must often be assumed that consent is not given voluntarily. Rather, the employee will regularly only give his consent because he fears reprisals from his employer. However voluntariness is  the essential part for consent to be effective. An involuntary consent obtained by means of open or covert threats or pressure is invalid and is deemed not to have been given.
We can therefore only use consent as a basis for voice recording if it can be absolutely guaranteed that a "no" from an employee will be taken into account without further problems.

# *Design of the recordings-process*
Based on different online-resources (free accessible webpages of llaw firms, consultants,…) we should also consider the design of the recording process
#* Recording should only permissible in individual cases, as occasional spot checks or on an occasion basis. In the training phase, more comprehensive measures are also permissible.
#* Proper information of the conversation partner (before the recording is starting)
#* Employees should always be informed in advance about each individual case. In exceptional cases, advance information from the employer that the employee is likely to be subject to checks in a limited period of time may be sufficient.
#* Furthermore, concrete upper numerical limits must be set in the call centre (e.g. 3 % of all calls made or a concrete sum of calls per month).
#* Records must be deleted immediately when they are no longer needed for the purpose for which they were created. It is best to implement fixed deletion routines here.

# *Criminal liability: Some attorneys explicitly mention the German criminal code*
§ 201 StGB Violation of the confidentiality of the word.
_"A custodial sentence not exceeding three years or a monetary penalty shall be imposed on anyone who without authorisation records the non-public spoken word of another person on a sound carrier or uses a recording made in this way or makes it accessible to a third party."_
They recommend that in order to avoid criminal liability when recording telephone calls in call centres, consent is therefore first required from both parties to the conversation. Both the call centre employee and the caller.

Hey Arsen! 👋 I’ve clarified the details for the topics you mentioned on your request. 🙂 

*Verification is stuck*

For verifications that are stuck, it depends on what is the error message that the user sees when tapping on the banner, and what is the user’s verification attempt status. In the example you shared, the user’s verification timed out, and we already have instructions in the KB article for that. 

The current instructions already include asking the user for an error message screenshot (or to simply explain what error message they see) and to review the verification attempt status. Overall, I don’t have sufficient information about this particular issue yet, so I can’t update the KB instructions. If you encounter more examples, do share with us anytime and we’ll look into it! 🙂 

*Receipt bulk download*

The Commerce team confirmed that it’s still not possible to download receipts in bulk - they have to be downloaded one by one. We don’t have information on whether this would change in the nearest future, but the Commerce team is aware of the inconveniences when processing bulk invoice requests at the moment.

I’ve created a task on our end to simplify the KB content related to issues with receipts (we’ll merge the [Car-sharing KB article|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360021441179] with the [Rider KB article|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/115003655854], and will list the correct article to follow in the [Car-sharing issues list|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360021033799]). Once this is completed, we’ll let everyone know via Slack. 🙂 

*Changing the marketing communications language*

The marketing communications (push notifications, in-app screens, emails) are available in each market’s most popular languages, and they’re sent based on what language the user has selected on their app. However, if the user has selected language that the particular market’s marketing comms don’t support, they’ll be sent in the default language (English).

* Let’s take an example:
** I’m in Latvia, so the marketing comms are likely available in Latvian, Russian, and English.
** If my app language is set to Latvian, I will receive marketing comms in Latvian.
** However, if I select, say, Estonian, I’ll receive them in English, as Estonian is not available for LV marketing comms.

I’ve created a task on our end to represent this information in the most relevant KB article. Once that’s done, we’ll post on Slack. 🙂

To have a clear division between skills and permissions: (mostly for myself)

*Permissions* - a data access control mechanism

*Skills* - a collection of possible CS agent attributes defining the kind of tasks they are capable of handling.

|SKILLS|PERMISSIONS|
|* Market (Estonia, United Kingdom, Poland etc)
* User persona (Rider, Eater etc)
* Issue type (Payments, Behaviour, Food Quality etc)
* Special skills (Safety, Social Media etc)|* Geography (city, country, region etc)
* Business vertical (Rides, Food, Rentals etc)
* User persona within vertical (Eater, Courier etc)
* Functional features (ability to refund an order, ability to unblock a driver etc)|

NB! We have admin {color:#ff5630}permissions{color} and admin {color:#ffbdad}roles{color}. *Permissions* relates to the admin functionality in order to perform certain actions, e.g blockings, editing profiles, etc. *Admin roles* refers to what permissions have been added to those roles. For example, _CS supply_ allows CS agents to perform admin actions that belong to OPS (e.g activating car profiles, etc).

Principles:

* instead of going through a list of country x persona configs and reject those that don’t match criteria
* go over countries x persona in dataset and only keep those that match criteria

Currently, in {{train}} step, the {{model_training.data_usable_for_forecasting(df_train)}} checks, for each country_x_persona, if the data is useable for forecasting.

country_x_persona is defined by product of two config matrix.

Two solutions:

* in train step, retrieve country_x_persona from {{df}}
** pros: 
*** avoid relying on static configs
** cons:
*** forces to still go over “unworthy” configurations in train step
* in pre-process step, retrieve and test for all country_x_persona from {{df}}
** pros:
*** if done early in pe-process, can save computing
*** slight save on space as we axe what we don’t need
** cons:
*** will loop through data twice, once during pre-processing, once during training

Remark:

* both these solutions remove the possibility to manually control what we see and what we don’t see in the forecast

We need to add a default value for the field {{expires_at}}

The DB servers have the {{explicit_defaults_for_timestamp}} disabled. This means that {{TIMESTAMP}} columns following the first one, must: *Explicitly allow* {{NULL}} *or have a* {{DEFAULT}} *value.* Otherwise, the automatic {{DEFAULT}} is {{'0000-00-00 00:00:00'}}

{noformat}mysql> SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'explicit_defaults_for_timestamp';
+---------------------------------+-------+
| Variable_name                   | Value |
+---------------------------------+-------+
| explicit_defaults_for_timestamp | OFF   |
+---------------------------------+-------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
{noformat}

 

The field {{expires_at}}:

* Is not the first {{TIMESTAMP}} type,
* It is declared as {{NOT NULL}}
* and it has no explicit {{DEFAULT}}

So MySQL automatically declared as {{DEFAULT '0000-00-00 00:00:00'}}.

_Please refer to_ [MySQL 5.7 Reference Manual :: sysvar_explicit_defaults_for_timestamp|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/server-system-variables.html#sysvar_explicit_defaults_for_timestamp]

 

With this, we hit another restriction:

The {{sql_mode}} in DB servers has includes {{NO_ZERO_DATE}}, which means that the {{DEFAULT '0000-00-00 00:00:00'}} is not a valid value.

{noformat}mysql> SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'sql_mode';
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Variable_name | Value                                                                                                                              |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| sql_mode      | IGNORE_SPACE,ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY,STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,NO_ZERO_DATE,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Hey, I’ll try to explain the logic we applied together with the Supportability team when the compensation guidelines were created:

*Vehicle ran out of battery*

We’re not talking about battery issues here, but simply cases where the vehicle’s battery runs empty. In reality, we shouldn’t issue any compensation at all because it’s the rider’s responsibility to check how much battery has left and they should plan their trip accordingly. Additionally, the vehicle doesn’t stop out of nowhere - the user is also warned before that the battery is too low. We still decided to compensate for the 1st time as a gesture of goodwill, but not for the 2nd time.

If you’re talking about cases where there’s a technical issue, this does not fall under this use case. I’m not sure how common these cases are, but it would be best to escalate such cases to the Tech Support team - if it is very common that the battery runs empty out of nowhere, it should be probably addressed and fixed, or if it cannot be fixed, we’d need to modify the compensation guidelines (but I’d need some examples, ideally Tech Support tickets). 

*Max order duration was met*

If you’re talking about cases where the trip was auto-finished in a restricted area, then we only refund the fine, not the whole trip. We decided to refund the fine because it’s not very convenient for the user to keep an eye on both the order duration and the zones - as far as I know, max order duration is currently not visible for the rider in the app, so they probably just don’t know what is the max time they can use the scooter and it can come as a surprise that the time is over. The battery percentage on the other hand is visible for them, so they should take that into account.

_What I see with tickets is that in restricted area the user cannot end the ride and the rider will run for another hour (max time). The user will also not receive a fine (or at least that's not clear in the order). —_ if the trip is finished in a restricted area, the user should receive the fine, which we should refund. If they didn’t receive the fine, then I’d say no compensation is necessary since they were still able to get from point A to point B, no? 

If the user was unable to finish the trip due to a technical issue: we issue a full refund to the user’s original payment method.

Let me know if this answers your question or if there are still some unclarities! 🙂

We need to add a default value for the field {{start_ts}}The DB servers have the {{explicit_defaults_for_timestamp}} disabled. This means that {{TIMESTAMP}} columns following the first one, must: *Explicitly allow* {{NULL}} *or have a* {{DEFAULT}} *value.* Otherwise, the automatic {{DEFAULT}} is {{'0000-00-00 00:00:00'}}

{noformat}mysql> SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'explicit_defaults_for_timestamp';
+---------------------------------+-------+
| Variable_name                   | Value |
+---------------------------------+-------+
| explicit_defaults_for_timestamp | OFF   |
+---------------------------------+-------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec){noformat}

The field {{start_ts}}:

* Is not the first {{TIMESTAMP}} type,
* It is declared as {{NOT NULL}}
* and it has no explicit {{DEFAULT}}

So MySQL automatically declared as {{DEFAULT '0000-00-00 00:00:00'}}.
_Please refer to_ [MySQL 5.7 Reference Manual :: sysvar_explicit_defaults_for_timestamp|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/server-system-variables.html#sysvar_explicit_defaults_for_timestamp]With this, we hit another restriction:
The {{sql_mode}} in DB servers has includes {{NO_ZERO_DATE}}, which means that the {{DEFAULT '0000-00-00 00:00:00'}} is not a valid value.

{noformat}mysql> SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'sql_mode';
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Variable_name | Value                                                                                                                              |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| sql_mode      | IGNORE_SPACE,ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY,STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,NO_ZERO_DATE,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec){noformat}

_Please refer to_ [MySQL 5.7 Reference Manual :: SQL Mode :: NO_ZERO_DATE|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/sql-mode.html#sqlmode_no_zero_date]An attempt to create the table as described above will fail with the following error: {{Error 1067: Invalid default value for 'start_ts'}}Possible solutions are:

# Explicitly declare a default non zero value i.e. {{expires_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP}}.
# Explicitly declared with the {{NULL}} attribute.

Summary:
The idea of the SPIKE was to identify if we would have any problem on applying the 3 rules for Pre-booked rides for all Scheduled Rides, making sure that requests created by the UI would already be a Pre-booked ride, once all requirements would always meet.

The main benefit is to made the transition for new markets transparent for the Agent, and at the same time avoid adding any limitation that would return errors from the BE.

Analysing the current scheduled rides that were created and actually finished we can see that:
1 - ~99% of the Scheduled Rides have a destination
2 - ~95% of the Scheduled Rides are created with Business Payments
3 - ~79% of the Scheduled Rides are created between 30 minutes and 72 hours


It sounds reasonable to apply the 1st and 2nd rules to all Scheduled Rides once we had less than 5% of all Scheduled Rides that did not follow them, and the benefits of restrictions it would be better for our long-term plan.

Restricting the 3rd rule on the other hand affects more than 20% of all Scheduled Rides, 17.5% being created in less than 30 min and 3% in more than 72 hours.

We can challenge on how useful it really is to create a Scheduled Rides that is scheduled for less than 30 min in the future, instead of just creating an on-demand, but an option to full-fill this requirement would be to get the available time-slot for scheduling a ride from the BE whenever the pickup stop is input.

Hello everyone,

As discussed via slack, the external counsel has reached an out-of-court settlement with the two co-defendants (Novo Rehum and Reby) and the 7 wokerts whereby:

# The workers expressly waive the action for NULLITY and PROTECTION of Fundamental Rights and the compensation for DAMAGES AND INJURY that they claimed in their lawsuits.
# Bolt, Novo Rehum and Reby acknowledge the unfairness of the implied dismissal and undertake to pay the following amounts:

* Bolt: EUR 8.853,77 
* Novo Rehum: EUR 16.229,25
* Reby EUR 12.541,51

With this settlement agreement, we have avoided the worst-case scenario indicated by our external lawyer, i.e.:

* Attending 7 hearings (one for each worker) with the consequent legal costs and the Court declaring that: i) Bolt has breached its obligation to subrogate the workers , ii) the dismissal is null and void for discrimination, so that iii) Bolt has to reinstate the workers + pay them their salaries and social security contributions since they were dismissed + an additional compensation for damages in the amount of 20,000 euros per worker.

According to our lawyer, the worst case scenario described above was likely to occur, given the tuitive nature of employment legislation in Spain and the new law passed in Spain to protect disabled workers against employment discrimination.

The aforementioned settlement agreements have been signed by all parties and are in the process of being homologated by the Court.

Current Escalation:

*Request Includes a Bolt User as a Suspect*

_Procedures for countries covered by the International CS Safety team_ 

If a DPA request sent to Bolt by the police contains a Bolt user as a suspect and the police are investigating a crime that was not yet known to Bolt and falls under one of Bolt’s [Event Categories|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1oAhKT6_oQo8MwLucW1W3go5LP6O-qQvFOfbr24sOdWA/edit#gid=680236715], after responding to the police, escalate the case to the International CS Safety team.

* The tool to log the police request should be triggered by the CS/OPS agent responding to the police.
* The same CS/OPS agent responding to the police can escalate the case to the in-house international CS Safety team, if needed by:
** Changing the safety level on Beehive to {{Severe}} (User Persona should still be {{Authority}}) 
** Leaving appropriate notes in the tool including:
*** Summary: Description of the incident in one or two sentences
*** Information provided: Yes/No
*** Investigation closed from Police: Yes/No
*** Possible Event Category: Suggested EC by CS/OPS
*** Next action: “IST please action”
** Selecting {{Escalate}} in the {{International Safety Team Review}} field
** Leaving the {{Has The Assessment Been Completed?}} field blank

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
If you choose {{Yes}} in {{Has The Assessment Been Completed?}}, it means that you do not need CS Safety assistance. The case won’t be escalated to the CS Safety team.
{panel}

Simpler query

{noformat}with active_supply as 
	(
		select 
			asc2.country_code,
			date(date_trunc('day', edha.period_local)) as period_date,
			count(distinct edha.driver_id) as active_supply
		from ng_public.etl_driver_hourly_activity edha 
		left join ng_public.admin_system_city asc2 on asc2.id = edha.city_id
		where edha.finished_orders > 0
			and asc2.country_code in ('gh', 'tz', 'az', 'ke', 'ng', 'za', 'py')
			and edha.period_local_date > date('2023-01-30')
		group by 1, 2
	),
	blocked_driver as 
	(
		select 
			country_code,
			date(date_trunc('day', hour_id)) as period_date,
			max(blocked_clients) as max_blocked_clients,
			avg(blocked_clients) as avg_blocked_clients
		from 
		(
			select 
				country as country_code,
				hour_id,
				sum(blocked_clients) as blocked_clients
			from ng_public.etl_billing_cashblock_driver_supply_impact
			where country in ('gh', 'tz', 'az', 'ke', 'ng', 'za', 'py')
			group by 1, 2
		)
		group by 1, 2
	),
	unioned as 
	(
		select 
			ass.country_code,
			ass.period_date,
			date_trunc('week', ass.period_date) as period_week,
			ass.active_supply,
			bd.avg_blocked_clients as blocked_clients
		from active_supply ass
		left join blocked_driver bd on bd.country_code = ass.country_code and bd.period_date = ass.period_date
	)
	select 
	*, blocked_clients/active_supply as blocked_to_active 
	from 
	(
		select 
			period_week,
			country_code,
			avg(active_supply) as active_supply,
			avg(blocked_clients) as blocked_clients
		from unioned
		group by 1,2
	)
	order by country_code, period_week desc{noformat}

Hey!

As background, GDPR foresees that consent needs to be a *freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous* indication of the data subject's (in this case driver) wishes by which he or she, by a statement or by a clear affirmative action, signifies agreement to the processing of personal data relating to him or her. On the basis of that, we need to make sure these conditions are fulfilled

* *freely given* - we are providing for this since we offer an alternative in the form of manual verification. However, we should transparently showcase these two options (currently, the manual option is in smaller letter, for example). This is an example how Uber is doing this, for background

!translation.jpg|width=41.666666666666664%!



* *specific, informed and unambiguous* - in order to fulfill this condition we propose the following wording which needs to actively agreed upon by driver (checking a box, for example)

_I consent to processing of my facial images (selfie and photo from identification document) for verification purposes by Bolt and authorized processors of Bolt. I am aware of my right to take back my consent via the Bolt app or by contacting Bolt’s customer support. Further information on the processing is provided in the Privacy Notice for Drivers._

*1. Question about the territorial scope of the data protection law*

Based on an English translation [(Data Guidance)|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1er528QMghJg8PiBlf6WX_9kmsZWyRH3-sd21WVfYhrQ/edit#heading=h.mt0d74ehhkc] and my very basic Portuguese skills:
The Data Protection Law is applicable whenever one of the following conditions is met:

* the data controller has its *head office in Angola* (Article 3(2)(a) of the Data Protection Law);
* the data processing takes place within the scope of the activities of a *data controller established in Angolan territory,* even if its head office is not located in Angola (Article 3(2)(b) of the Data Protection Law);
* the data processing takes place o*utside of Angola in a place where Angolan law applies* pursuant to international public or private law (Article 3(2)(c) of the Data Protection Law); and
* the data controller *uses means located in Angolan territory during the course of the data processing* (Article 3(2)(d) of the Data Protection Law).

Article 3(3) of the Data Protection Law sets out that the controller is deemed to have *recourse to means situated in Angolan territory* when the personal data processing operations are carried out using means situated in Angolan territory or the personal data is hosted in the Angolan territory, it sufficing, for the purposes of the Data Protection Law, that such *means be merely used for the collection, recording, or transit of personal data within or through the territory of the Republic of Angola.*

_“Unfortunately, no definition of 'means' is provided. Thus, there is a risk that this word encompasses infrastructures such as servers located in Angola or any agencies, affiliates, representatives, employees, or service providers located in Angola through which a foreign data controller collects or processes data. Therefore, a data controller that has no presence in Angola may still have to abide by the terms of the Data Protection Law even if the data processing operation it wishes to undertake only involves using servers that operate in Angola as a way to transfer data from one country to the other or if its business structure involves using a representative, agency, or another type of service provider located in Angola to collect data or to act as a data processor for it.” (Data guidance)_

→ We won’t be established in Angola, no employees, no infrastructure, but of course we collect personal data. Are we considering collecting data by the mobil device of the user as “*means located in Angolan territory”*
If yes (I would), look at Nr. 2
