*2. If the Data Protection Law (Angola) is applicable*
*Requirement*
-{color:#ff5630} *Declaration - Processing activities:* {color}According to Article 35(1) of the Data Protection Law, data processing requires either prior notification to the APD or authorisation from the same. In the first case, upon receiving a notification, the APD has a period of 30 days to respond. Once this period has elapsed, the data processing operation is considered to have been duly notified and can take place (Article 35(2) of the Data Protection Law).
- {color:#ff991f}*Declaration - Cross boarder transfer:*{color} For international data transfers the rules and principles applicable to a transfer of personal data from Angola to a foreign country will depend on whether the APD deems the country to which the data is to be transferred to provide an 'adequate level of protection'.

If it does, then the transfer of data will only require a notification to the APD, and if it does not, then the data controller must obtain prior authorisation from the APD. 
*_Authorisation_* will be granted in the cases specified in Article 34 of the Data Protection Law, including:

* where the data subject has given express given consent;
* where the transfer is necessary to execute a contract to which the data subject is part of or to carry out preliminary steps before executing a contract with the data subject;
* where the intended recipient of the data in the relevant country enters into a contract with the data controller and undertakes to provide an adequate level of protection for the data; and
* where the transfer is to another company in one particular corporate group which has implemented binding corporate rules on the privacy and protection of personal data.

- *Declaration-template ont the homepage of the DPA*


- {color:#bf2600}*Need of an representative established in Angola*{color}

If a data processing operation falls under the scope of the Data Protection Law, the data controller, through communication with the APD, must nominate a representative established in Angola in order to delegate all of its rights and obligations under the Data Protection Law, as stated in Article 3(4).

Our general approach has been the following:

* Changes to individual pricing elements only (e.g. pick up fee, per km surcharge etc.) - no need for 15 days notice *unless* the changes have a significant negative impact on courier earnings (obviously this is subjective, so we would need to exercise discretion but we would expect such cases would be rare). To be clear, we should still communicate the changes regardless of the impact, but we can do this without 15 days’ notice.
* Changes to the broader formula of courier earnings:
* 1. If these have a positive effect for courier earnings, no need to notify couriers of the change.

* 2. If these have a negative or mixed impact on courier earnings - *we should give 15 days notice of any changes in this instance.*
* Any grey areas / corner cases - we would likely need to address these on a case by case basis.

{code:sql}WITH quick_change AS (
SELECT a.meta.order_id AS order_id,
a.meta.city_id AS city_id
FROM archive_analytical.user_destination_update a
JOIN ng_public.company_order_try ot ON a.meta.order_id = ot.order_id AND a.meta.city_id = ot.city_id AND ot.state = 'finished'
JOIN ng_public.company_order_try_state_log ot2 ON ot.id = ot2.order_try_id AND a.meta.city_id = ot2.city_id AND ot2.to_state = 'driver_accepted' 
JOIN archive_analytical.driver_order_price_check pc ON pc.meta.order_id = ot.order_id AND pc.meta.city_id = ot.city_id
WHERE a.created_hour >= date '2023-01-01'
AND pc.created_hour >= date '2023-01-01'
AND ot.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
AND ot2.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
AND a.decision.decision = 'pass'
AND date_diff('second',ot2.created,a.created) < 0 
AND (CAST(json_extract_scalar(pc.input, '$.additional.historical_route.total_approved_change_destination_count') AS bigint) > 0 OR json_extract_scalar(pc.input, '$.additional.last_updated_prediction.price') IS NOT NULL)
AND a.meta.city_id IN (438,1398,839,840,1431,687,817,816,386,815,835,836,437,812,457) -- PT cities
GROUP BY 1,2 
) 
SELECT 
APPROX_DISTINCT(co.order_id,0.0041) AS total_orders,
APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN co.fraud_label THEN co.order_id END,0.0041) AS fraud_orders, 
ROUND(APPROX_DISTINCT(CASE WHEN co.fraud_label THEN co.order_id END,0.0041)*1.00/APPROX_DISTINCT(co.order_id,0.0041),2) AS fraud_ratio,
ROUND(SUM(CAST(co.user_price_eur AS double)),2) AS total_sum,
COALESCE(ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.fraud_label THEN CAST(co.user_price_eur AS double) END),2),0) AS total_fraud_sum,
ROUND(ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.fraud_label THEN CAST(co.user_price_eur AS double) END),2)*1.00/ROUND(SUM(CAST(co.user_price_eur AS double)),2),2) AS amount_ratio
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
JOIN quick_change qc ON qc.order_id = co.order_id AND qc.city_id = co.city_id 
WHERE co.created_date >= date '2023-01-01'
AND co.order_type = 'rides'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND co.payment_method_type NOT IN ('business','default'){code}

Hi Mariann, thanks for reaching out. To answer your questions:

# Yes the prices and discounts from the app can be displayed in the newsletter, provided they are still applicable for a reasonable period of time after the newsletter is sent out. If I understand correctly, the newsletter would show the pricing at a particular point in time, so we should be careful to ensure that the prices displayed are actually available to customers who try to make a purchase afterwards. If the prices are only available for a limited time then we should make it clear that the offer is time-limited.

Wherever we are displaying a price reduction (e.g. was X now &, or -X% etc.) we need to include the lowest 30 day price. We have an automated tool which ensures the lowest 30 day price is automatically displayed on the app, so provided this is where the prices are taken from for the newsletter then I don’t see any additional risk here.

# The wording of the disclaimer depends on the particular offer - the important thing is that we communicate any key conditions or exclusions that may apply. The example you shared looks good to me, but it would depend on the particular conditions that are relevant for each offer so it’s difficult to generalise.


I hope this helps clear things up. Please let me know if you have any other questions.
